prototype: research/zk-membership (guest v2: forward-private nullifiers, action binding)
statement: Knowledge of x with SHA-256('avpn/member/v2'||H^(N-k)(x)) a leaf of a tree of 2^20 commitments, H(x)=SHA-256('avpn/fp-step/v1'||x); nullifier SHA-256('avpn/nullifier/v2'||x||epoch||scope); public: root, lifetime N, start epoch, epoch, scope, action, nullifier
machine: Intel Core i7-8565U (2018 laptop, 4 cores / 8 threads), 15 GiB RAM, CPU proving only (no GPU)
checks: fresh nullifier next epoch, after stepping the secret forward
a later epoch's secret cannot prove an earlier epoch (forward privacy)
a proof cannot be moved to another action
distinct members: distinct nullifiers, same root
outsider cannot produce the members' root
journal carries neither the secret nor the leaf
zkvm: risc0-zkvm 3.1 (STARK over BabyBear, FRI; succinct receipt, no SNARK wrapper)
notes: Real proofs: the host refuses RISC0_DEV_MODE (which fakes them) and asserts a succinct receipt.
prove_seconds is the first of six proofs; the run's six took 2986 s in all, about 8 minutes each.

Measured under memory pressure: the prover used about 8.8 GiB with 8 GiB of the machine in swap, and the desktop and browser kept running. The times are an upper bound; how much of the rise over v1 is the 360 in-proof chain steps and how much is memory pressure is not separated.
tree_build_seconds rose because every leaf now commits to the end of its member's 365-step chain (about 383 million SHA-256 calls for 2^20 members), host side only.
The succinct receipt is one STARK (hash-based, post-quantum). RISC Zero's Groth16 wrapper would shrink it to a few hundred bytes but rests on elliptic curves, so it is not used.
